outcome: Help teachers prepare high-quality, curriculum-aligned lessons and differentiated resources faster.
overview: Teachers rebuild similar lesson plans, activities and communications across disconnected repositories, and some reach for unapproved public AI tools. This solution provides a governed copilot that retrieves approved curriculum, institutional templates and licensed resources, then drafts lesson plans, differentiated activities, rubrics and parent communications in Arabic and English — every draft carrying citations back to its sources. Teachers remain the authors and approve every output before it reaches a learner or a learning platform. A 6–10-week pilot with one department measures preparation time saved, citation coverage and template compliance against an agreed baseline, targeting at least a 25% reduction in approved lesson-preparation time.

benefits.source: Redington Education catalogue; to validate against a six-week effort baseline
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on repository quality and teacher adoption — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Keep every generated draft attributable — 100% source citations from approved repositories
benefits.source: Reference design — retrieval is allowlisted to approved sources with enforced citations
benefits.limits: Holds for the governed assistant only; content pasted from elsewhere is out of scope

benefits.text: Cut duplicated teaching assets and improve template compliance across departments
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Measured on the pilot department’s repositories; requires curriculum metadata upkeep

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (UAE, KSA); institutional content and prompts stay in the customer tenancy in the reference designs

notFor.situation: No controlled content repository or curriculum ownership
notFor.why: The copilot only retrieves from approved, rights-cleared sources; without them it has nothing safe to ground drafts in

notFor.situation: The institution wants uncited open-web generation for teaching materials
notFor.why: Provenance and copyright control are the point of the governed design — removing citations removes the safety case

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the institution owns curriculum, content rights and acceptable-use policy · Duration: 6–10 weeks pilot; 12–20 weeks to scaled deployment
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, retrieval engineer, evaluation designer; customer curriculum owner, repository administrator, information-security reviewer, teacher champions · Support model: Business-hours support with term-time escalation cover; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Source and rights audit
2) Retrieval index build
3) Template and evaluation design
4) Teacher co-design sessions
5) Security and accessibility testing
6) Controlled rollout and benefit review

Curriculum alignment confirmed by the curriculum owner

Teacher edit and approval workflow proven, with safe failure on low-confidence drafts
Measured preparation-time saving reported against the baseline
